note: Developer labels on the stored official texts and the synthetic pilot profiles and registers. INDICATIVE only: not expert gold, one reader, no adjudication. No label is copied from a model or from the rule reader. Clauses of the DEV split were read while the wording rules were being corrected against them, so a score on DEV measures fit, not accuracy; the HOLDOUT clauses were labelled from the text before any reader was run on them and no rule was changed after they were scored. UNDECIDED marks a clause the developer could not classify; it is scored in no task. Label corrections made after a first scoring are listed under label_changes, with the score before them.

label_changes.why: entity-level sides whose entity also holds products the duty does not reach (an alcohol-free beer next to the beers, an energy drink next to colas and water): the routing word for that is PARTIAL, as in BEVERAGE_TR_DEV_V1; the developer had written APPLIES. No routing rule was changed for these cases.
a second defensible reading was admitted next to the first (see the two clauses with two addressee labels set in the builder)

kinds.OBLIGATION: a positive duty of a company or a requirement on its product or label
kinds.PROHIBITION: something a company may not do
kinds.BOTH: one clause that states a duty and a prohibition
kinds.AUTHORITY: a task or a power of an authority, or a delegation to secondary rules
kinds.STATEMENT: definition, scope, classification, deeming, or a fragment with no predicate
kinds.REFERENCE: makes another text or provision applicable; scored in no duty task
